description: Preparers enter source data and prepare Form 1040 series returns; reviewers check and approve; includes AI-assisted data entry (AI-001)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Peak-season values (February 1 to April 15 and October 1 to 15): about $340,000 of individual tax work per business day; a lost day in the last week before a deadline cannot be made up; vendor SaaS RPO 1 h
manual_workaround: File extensions (Form 4868) early for unfinished clients; prioritize by deadline; remote work from any office or home
dependent_people_or_facilities: Preparers and reviewers; Offices 1-6 or remote
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,700 individual returns completed per peak business day; 11,000 in the last 5 business days before April 15
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late-filed returns trigger failure-to-file penalties charged to clients; engagement letters commit the Company to reimburse penalties caused by its own delay
client_harm_impact: Moderate: penalties, delayed refunds, and extension stress for clients; no physical harm
deadline_or_contract_driver: IRS filing deadlines (April 15; October 15 for extended returns)

business_process: Business, trust, and exempt-organization return preparation
description: Prepare partnership, S corporation, C corporation, fiduciary, and exempt-organization returns and related state returns
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Peak in the weeks before March 15, April 15, September 15, and October 15: about $190,000 of business tax work per business day; K-1s feed individual returns, so delays cascade
manual_workaround: File extensions for unfinished entities; prioritize entities whose K-1s are needed by individual clients
dependent_people_or_facilities: Business tax teams; Offices 1-6 or remote
quantified_operational_impact: About 300 business returns completed per peak business day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late partnership and S corporation returns carry per-partner and per-shareholder monthly penalties charged to clients
client_harm_impact: Moderate: penalties and late K-1s for owners
deadline_or_contract_driver: IRS filing deadlines (March 15 and April 15; extended September 15 and October 15)

description: Release signed returns for e-file through the tax software vendor; track IRS and state acknowledgments and rejects; weekly EFIN and PTIN checks
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Returns must be transmitted by the deadline and acknowledgments prove timely filing; the vendor transmits (vendor SaaS RPO 1 h)
manual_workaround: Extensions through the vendor or IRS e-file; paper filing with proof of mailing as a last resort
dependent_third_parties: Tax software vendor (Authorized IRS e-file transmitter); IRS and state e-file systems
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,900 federal and state transmissions per peak business day across 6 EFINs
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missed transmission on a deadline day means late filing for every unsent return
client_harm_impact: Severe for clients on deadline day: penalties and delayed refunds
deadline_or_contract_driver: IRS and state e-file deadlines; Pub. 1345 ERO duties

description: Receive source documents through the portal, mail, and drop-off at 6 offices; scan and index at the document processing center; file to the DMS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Preparers stall without documents; clients keep originals so lost scans can be re-collected; DMS backed up daily (RPO 24 h); portal vendor retains uploads
manual_workaround: Preparers work directly from portal uploads and paper originals; scanning shifts to Offices 2-6
dependent_people_or_facilities: Document processing center staff (about 30 in season); Office 1
quantified_operational_impact: About 9,000 documents scanned per peak business day
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; backlog raises late-filing risk

description: Clients sign Forms 8879 and engagement letters and download returns in the portal; IRC 7216 consents captured
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The ERO may not transmit until Form 8879 is signed (IRS Pub. 1345); wet signature fallback exists
manual_workaround: Wet-signature Form 8879 in person or by mail; paper returns; paper consent forms
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,500 signatures per peak business day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Transmission without a signed Form 8879 breaches e-file rules; consent captured late breaches 301.7216-3(b)(1)

description: About 30 vendor staff outside the United States prepare first drafts of individual returns in firm-hosted virtual desktops; Company reviewers finish them
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Offshore staff prepare about 5,500 first drafts a season (15% of individual returns); U.S. staff can absorb 3 days with overtime
manual_workaround: Reassign drafts to U.S. preparers and seasonal staff with overtime; file extensions for the rest
dependent_systems: SYS-04 virtual desktop pool; SYS-01; SYS-03; SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Offshore preparation support vendor; cloud provider
quantified_operational_impact: About 250 first drafts per peak business day
quantified_regulatory_impact: A restart must keep SSN masking and consent checks in place (26 CFR 301.7216-3(b)(4))

business_process: IRS and state notice response and representation
description: Respond to IRS and state notices and examinations for clients within notice deadlines
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most notices allow 30 days or more and can be extended by phone
manual_workaround: Call the agency for more time; work from paper copies
quantified_operational_impact: About 120 open notices at any time
quantified_regulatory_impact: Missed notice deadlines can lose appeal rights for clients
client_harm_impact: Moderate if appeal rights are lost; rare

description: Plan, perform, and document attest engagements in the workpaper application; journal entry analytics (AI-004)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Report dates are set by lenders, boards, and grantors, usually with some slack; workpaper server backed up daily (RPO 24 h)
manual_workaround: Work offline in local engagement files; reschedule fieldwork; request lender extensions
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,000 engagements a year; about 25 report releases per week in peak months
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late reports can breach loan covenants and grant reporting dates for clients
client_harm_impact: Moderate: client covenant and grant issues
deadline_or_contract_driver: Client report deadlines (lender covenants, single audit due dates)

description: Perform SOC 1 and SOC 2 examinations for service organization clients and issue reports and bridge letters
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Report delivery dates are contractual; bridge letters can cover short delays
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late SOC reports delay clients' own customer and auditor commitments

description: Run payroll for about 210 business clients (about 8,600 client employees) on the payroll processing service; payroll tax deposits and filings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Each payroll has a fixed pay date and a processing cutoff 1 to 2 business days earlier; missing it means client employees are not paid on time; vendor SaaS RPO 1 h
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the vendor support line; manual checks for terminated employees; vendor emergency processing
quantified_operational_impact: About 40 payroll runs per business day; peak on the 15th and last day of each month
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late payroll tax deposits bring penalties charged to clients; late wages breach state wage payment laws for client employers
client_harm_impact: Severe: client employees not paid on payday
deadline_or_contract_driver: Client pay dates; federal and state payroll tax deposit schedules

description: Record transactions, reconcile accounts, approve and release vendor payments for about 340 business clients
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Bill pay runs twice weekly; client month-end closes allow a few days of slack; vendor SaaS
manual_workaround: Clients pay urgent bills directly; defer month-end close
dependent_third_parties: Cloud accounting vendor; bill-pay vendor; banks
quantified_operational_impact: About 2,600 vendor payments released per week
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late payments may incur client late fees; no regulatory deadline
client_harm_impact: Moderate: late vendor payments for clients

description: Transaction advisory, valuation, and outsourced CFO work using client data rooms and firm files
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deadlines are set with clients and can usually move by days; transaction dates are the exception
manual_workaround: Work from local files; ask clients for short extensions

description: Email, phones, and portal messages with clients, the IRS, and state agencies
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deadline questions and document requests peak in season; email is also the BEC attack path; mailbox data kept by the vendor
manual_workaround: Phone tree; website notice; portal messages; temporary clean mailboxes after a BEC
quantified_operational_impact: About 45,000 client emails per peak week
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; delays raise late-filing risk
client_harm_impact: Moderate: clients cannot reach the Company

description: Time-based and fixed-fee invoicing, client payments through the hosted payment page, and collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $400,000 of receipts per business day on average; invoices can be delayed a few days; vendor SaaS retains data
manual_workaround: Manual invoices; pay by check or wire with call-back verification
quantified_operational_impact: About $1.2 million of cash delayed at MTD

description: Single sign-on, MFA, conditional access, and account changes for every system
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every process depends on sign-in; an outage stops all SaaS access; vendor SaaS
manual_workaround: Break-glass accounts (exist for the cloud only; planned for the identity provider and productivity suite)
dependent_people_or_facilities: IT operations; Director of Information Security
quantified_operational_impact: All 600 employees and seasonal staff blocked

description: Firm payroll, onboarding and termination (including about 130 seasonal staff and interns), and recruiting with the applicant tracking system (AI-005)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; seasonal onboarding peaks in January; termination drives access removal
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider; manual onboarding checklist
quantified_operational_impact: About 130 seasonal and intern hires each January
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late wages to employees; delayed termination leaves access open

business_process: Practice management, scheduling, and engagement letters
description: Client onboarding, engagement letters and IRC 7216 consents, staff scheduling, and time capture
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Engagement letters and consents must exist before work starts; vendor SaaS retains data
manual_workaround: Paper engagement letters and consents; spreadsheets for scheduling
quantified_operational_impact: About 800 engagement letters a week in January
quantified_regulatory_impact: Work or disclosures without a signed consent breach 26 CFR 301.7216-3

business_process: Security monitoring and incident response (enabling service)
description: EDR and SIEM monitoring by the MSSP; triage and escalation; incident response
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without monitoring, attacks during an outage go unseen; recovery cannot be validated; SIEM vendor SaaS
manual_workaround: Security engineers watch EDR and identity consoles directly on extended hours
quantified_operational_impact: Detection coverage for 776 endpoints and 14 SaaS and cloud services
quantified_regulatory_impact: Delayed discovery can shorten the time left on the FTC 30-day and Florida 30-day clocks
